courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: We got errors because I changed the user isAuthenticated and userId and therefore in places where we
used these fields, we now have problems,
for example in the booking service. If we have a look at the booking service, there we have an error where
I extract the userId and that makes sense,
the userId is no longer a string I can just pass here as an argument, instead in the auth service,
I changed my userId to essentially return an observable and therefore, we need to change the way
we extract it here. When we need that userId, we need to reach out to the auth service which we already
do
but then on the userId here, we simply need to subscribe
and of course I don't want to set up an ongoing subscription but I want to get exactly the latest snapshot.
So I'll add the pipe method here and then the take operator which you therefore need to import from rxjs
operators in case you're not doing that already
and then here, I want to take exactly one value and in here,
I then get my userId which is that string and if we're not getting a userId,
so if this is null for some reason, I want to return and not continue,
otherwise I can now create my new booking here and there,
we now have that userId field.
The problem we now have is that I create that new booking in the subscribe method of my subscription
to userId and I then want to use that here in this HTTP request which is another observable chain.
If I leave the code like this, this will not work because we already see it here, new booking is not available
there and even if we would define it as a variable that is available everywhere, even then, the order
of execution would be incorrect because this is an asynchronous task here and therefore this would
not be finished before this executes.
So we actually have to move this into our observable chain
we have up there and hence, I will actually not subscribe here but use a switch map because that allows
me to convert one observable, my userId observable into a different one which will be this HTTP request
observable down there.
So here in this switch map, I now get my userId just as before in the subscription and I will move
the entire code I had into there and now in there, I will return this observable where I send a post
request, I return this after creating the new booking and now we can add the operators we had on that
observable chain simply to that pipe method we had up there, like this. Now the one thing that is now problematic
is the new booking which now is available up there but not down here where I need to get the ID of that
booking or where I want to set it and for that, well we simply can define let new booking up there
as a variable which eventually will hold a booking and then I just don't create a constant
here but assign this to my booking, to my new booking.
Now this might look very complicated but in the end what I did here is simply create a new observable
chain where I first of all get my userId, once to get the latest snapshot and then I return nothing
if we have no userId which actually would be invalid code because switch map always needs to have
an observable return.
So indeed I will not return nothing here but actually throw a new error, no userId found, so that
we really have an error in the application and therefore make it into the error handler of that observable
chain
but we should have a userId by default and then I create a new booking. I use that in that HTTP request
which I then return in this switch map because switch map is an operator that gives us the result of
one observable and returns a new observable and then we have other operators that pick up on that returned
response by that observable and do the same we did before. Now we've fixed the booking file, in the discover
page we have another issue and there, I also have the issue of me using the userId which now is no
longer a string but an observable.
Now let's also fix that.
